title: Investigating Social Bias Changes in Quantized Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2602.06181v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Post-training quantization reduces the memory needed to run large language models but alters their social biases in ways that aggregate metrics fail to capture. We present the first large-scale study of 50 quantized models evaluated on PostTrainingBiasBench, a unified benchmark of 13 closed- and open-ended bias datasets. We identify a phenomenon we term quantization-induced bias flipping, in which quantization causes models to change responses from biased to unbiased and vice versa, up to 21% of the time, despite no change in aggregate bias scores. These flips are strongly associated with model uncertainty, where the responses with high uncertainty are 3-11x more likely to change than the confident ones. Quantization strength amplifies this effect, with 4-bit quantized models exhibiting 4-6x more behavioral changes than 8-bit quantized models. translated_title: 研究量化语言模型中的社会偏见变化
translated_abstract: 后训练量化减少了运行大型语言模型所需的内存，但会以聚合指标无法捕捉的方式改变模型的社会偏见。我们首次对50个量化模型进行了大规模研究，在PostTrainingBiasBench上进行评估，该基准统一整合了13个封闭式和开放式偏见数据集。我们发现了一种被称为“量化诱导偏见翻转”的现象：量化会导致模型的回复在有偏见与无偏见之间发生改变，比例高达21%，而总体偏见分数却没有任何变化。这些翻转与模型不确定性密切相关，高不确定性的回复发生变化的概率是高置信度回复的3至11倍。量化强度会放大这一效应，4位量化模型表现出的行为变化是8位量化模型的4至6倍。关键的是，这些变化在不同人口群体间造成了不对称的影响。
tldr: 该论文首次大规模研究发现，量化会诱导语言模型的社会偏见发生“翻转”（回复在有偏见与无偏见之间互换，比例高达21%），这种变化在总体指标中不可见，与模型不确定性密切相关，并随量化强度增强而放大，从而对不同人口群体产生不对称影响。
en_tdlr: This first large-scale study reveals that quantization induces "bias flipping" in language models—swapping responses between biased and unbiased up to 21% of the time despite unchanged aggregate bias scores—with flips strongly tied to model uncertainty, amplified by stronger quantization, and creating asymmetric impacts across demographic groups.
